reference.capture: public UILabel geometry and Core Animation model/presentation layers sampled by CADisplayLink

minimization.automaticRestoration: scroll reversal restores chrome away from the content edge
minimization.atScrollEdgeRestoration: reversal away from the top keeps chrome hidden; pulling through the top gradually restores it
minimization.progress: scroll-driven; no constant animation duration was measured

rendererFits.method: damped response fit to effective presentation opacity; the 15-point translation follows the same measured progress
rendererFits.provenance: These are fitted renderer inputs, not recovered native algorithms or intercepted SwiftUI spring constructors. Each capture has subframe onset uncertainty.

titleTypography.provenance: Flutter system-font aliases and tracking validated against native label geometry; not inferred native font construction.

rendererFits.regressionAlignment: Shared onset derived from the directly captured large-title ease-in-out opacity animation; inline data includes its onset lag.

limits: ToolbarTitleAlignment requires iOS 27.2; available simulators run iOS 27.0/27.1. Explicit alignment follows the public API contract, with RTL/layout tests, rather than a runnable 27.2 native comparison.
Automatic minimization keeps the non-minimizing default. Native searchable toolbarPrincipal integration is not inferred from arbitrary Flutter widgets.
At-scroll-edge restoration uses the content's top in Flutter. UIKit's overscroll/inset feedback and momentum through that edge are not reproduced exactly.
SwiftUI inlineLarge was captured as an additional reference; it is not a new implicit title duplication API in this release.

impellerOpacityComparison.note: Native presentation trace vs rendered Flutter frames, shared large-title onset; one representative slow transition each, both scaffold/sliver.
